{{< include _snippets/agent_intro.md >}}

The agent runs the `dsh` headless profile, which is DeepSeek Harness's complete coding-agent composition (system prompt, file/shell/search tools, subagents, workflows, todo and goal tracking, automatic compaction), with its DeepSeek Messages adapter pointed at the Inspect model bridge.

## Options

The following options are supported for customizing the behavior of the agent:

| Option | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `system_prompt` | Additional system prompt (prepended to the task, as `dsh` headless has no separate system-prompt option). |
| `skills` | Additional [skills](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/tools-standard.html#sec-skill) to make available to the agent. |
| `mcp_servers` | MCP servers (see [MCP Servers](#mcp-servers) below for details, including which servers are accepted). |
| `bridged_tools` | Host-side Inspect tools to expose via MCP (see [Bridged Tools](#bridged-tools) below for details). |
| `mcp_ready_timeout` | Seconds to wait for bridged MCP endpoints to serve tools before the agent launch errors. |
| `attempts` | Allow the agent to have multiple scored attempts at solving the task. |
| `model` | Model name to use for agent (defaults to main model for task). |
| `context_window` | Context window to configure for `dsh` (drives its automatic compaction, see [Compaction](#compaction)). Defaults to the bridged model's context length from Inspect model metadata, falling back to `dsh`'s own default (1,000,000 tokens) when that metadata is unavailable. |
| `filter` | Filter for intercepting bridged model requests. |
| `retry_refusals` | Should refusals be retried? (pass number of times to retry) |
| `cwd` | Working directory for {{< meta agent_name >}} session. |
| `env` | Environment variables to set for {{< meta agent_name >}}. These are visible to the model (its shell tool can print them). |
| `version` | Version of {{< meta agent_name >}} to use (see [Installation](#installation) below for details) |

: {tbl-colwidths=\[25,75\]}

For example, here we specify a custom system prompt:

```python
{{< meta agent >}}(
    system_prompt="You are an ace system researcher."
)
```

{{< include _snippets/agent_mcp_servers.md >}}

{{< meta agent_name >}} supports stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP servers. Per-server tool filtering (`tools=[...]`) and legacy SSE servers are not supported and raise an error.

### Credentials

`dsh`'s own tools (its shell tool in particular) run as the same user as `dsh`, so the model can read anything `dsh` can: its configuration files, its environment, and the files and descriptors it has open (through `/proc`). Nothing handed to `dsh` inside the sandbox can be kept from the model, so:

-   An HTTP MCP server with `headers` (e.g. an `Authorization` token), or with a user or password in its URL, is rejected with an error. To give the agent tools that need a credential, connect to the server on the host and pass the tools with `bridged_tools`: they are served to `dsh` by the model bridge, and the credential never enters the sandbox.

-   Everything else in an MCP server's configuration is written to `dsh`'s profile in the sandbox, so treat it as visible to the model, like `env`: an HTTP server's URL (query string included), and a stdio server's command, arguments and `env`. A stdio server also runs inside the sandbox.

The only key `dsh` is given for inference is a dummy one for the model bridge.

{{< include _snippets/agent_bridged_tools.md >}}

## Sub-Agents

`dsh` can delegate: its `subagent` tool starts a fresh child agent, `subagent_fork` one that inherits the conversation so far, and `send_message` gives a child that has finished more work. Every child runs in the background. The call returns as soon as the child has started, and its answer reaches the parent later as a notice.

Each child's model calls are recorded in a transcript span of its own, so the viewer shows the root agent's conversation and each child's as separate lanes. A child's span opens when the parent's call is made and closes when the parent receives the child's finishing notice, not when the call returns. A child resumed with `send_message` continues in a new span with the same name.

The sample's messages and output are the root agent's conversation and its last answer, whichever agent made the last model call. (If a request's sender can't be told after the root's last answer, which classification reports as `"unknown"`, the conversation the model bridge tracked is used instead.)

Bridged requests are classified so that a `filter` can tell them apart (`is_root_agent()`, `current_agent_bridge_context()`): see [Sub-Agent Context](sub-agent-context.qmd) for what is detected and its limits.

## Compaction

`dsh` condenses the conversation itself when it nears the context window, with a separate model call. That call is classified `"utility"` and marked in the transcript by a `CompactionEvent` (source `deepseek_harness`).

`dsh` starts compacting at 80% of `context_window`, or earlier if the window minus the model's output limit minus a 65,536-token reserve is smaller. The agent passes the output limit from Inspect's model metadata; for a model without one `dsh` assumes 256,000 tokens. When the window cannot fit the output limit plus the reserve, `dsh` does not compact ahead of time and only reacts to a context-overflow error from the model.

## Model Bridging

`dsh` speaks DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible Messages API. A few adjustments keep a bridged run close to a native `dsh` run against DeepSeek's API:

-   **Reasoning replay.** The bridge can only return reasoning to an Anthropic-style client as a `thinking` block when it came from Inspect's Anthropic provider; reasoning from any other provider (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, etc.) would reach `dsh` as plain `<think>` text and be sent back to the model as visible output. The agent restores those blocks to the original reasoning (including provider signatures, e.g. OpenRouter `reasoning_details`) before each request, so the model sees its earlier reasoning as reasoning, as it would natively.

-   **Model identity.** `dsh` is given the served model's real name, so its system prompt names the actual model. The model is registered as a plain (text-only) catalog entry: the built-in DeepSeek entries opt into DeepSeek-API-only wire features (in-history system prompt updates, deferred tool loading, Files API image upload) that the bridge does not speak.

-   **Reasoning effort.** Natively `dsh` requests `high` reasoning effort. The bridge doesn't forward the inner agent's request-level settings, so the agent applies `reasoning_effort="high"` itself unless the eval sets `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_tokens`, or a `reasoning` field in `extra_body` (e.g. `--extra-body '{"reasoning":{"effort":"max"}}'` to request `max` through OpenRouter, where Inspect currently sends `reasoning_effort="max"` as `xhigh`).

-   **Upstream reporting is disabled.** Telemetry export, the session-log and plugin-inventory fields that `dsh` attaches to requests for DeepSeek's official API, and the auxiliary model call that titles the session are turned off.

-   **Web search.** `dsh`'s `web_search` tool is pointed at its Messages-based search provider, which makes a model request of its own carrying Anthropic's `web_search` server tool. That request goes to the bridge and is served by the agent's model: it returns results when the model's provider supports Inspect's internal web search (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity); otherwise (e.g. DeepSeek models) the tool reports an error to the model. The request is classified `"utility"`. `web_fetch` runs from inside the sandbox and is subject to its network policy.

-   **Goals are switched off.** `dsh`'s goal tools (`create_goal`, `get_goal`, `update_goal`) keep a session working across automatic continuation rounds. Its one-shot headless mode doesn't wait for those rounds: with a goal active it exits with an error as the next round starts, after a turn that completed. The tools are therefore not offered to the model.

-   **Permissions.** `dsh` runs in `danger-full-access` mode (no approval prompts) since the sandbox is the isolation boundary.

## Installation

{{< meta agent_name >}} publishes its standalone runtime (a single native executable, with no Node.js or Python requirement in the sandbox) as glibc-only Linux wheels of the [`deepseek-harness-runtime-bin`](https://pypi.org/project/deepseek-harness-runtime-bin/) PyPI package, and the agent runs it via `bash`, so sandbox images must provide glibc 2.28+ and bash (e.g. Debian/Ubuntu based images). musl-based images such as Alpine are not supported and fail at version resolution time.

By default, the agent will download the current latest version of {{< meta agent_name >}} and copy it to the sandbox. You can override this behaviour using the `version` option:

| Option | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `"auto"` | Use any available version of {{< meta agent_name >}} in the sandbox, otherwise download the latest version. |
| `"sandbox"` | Use the version of {{< meta agent_name >}} in the sandbox (raises `RuntimeError` if not available in the sandbox) |
| `"latest"` | Download and use the very latest version. |
| `"x.x.x"` | Download and use a specific version number (a `deepseek-harness-runtime-bin` PyPI version, e.g. `"0.2.1rc2"`). |

: {tbl-colwidths=\[25,75\]}

{{< meta agent_name >}} is in developer preview and documents that it will make compatibility-breaking changes, so pinning a specific version is recommended for reproducible evaluations.

## Not Supported

-   **Centaur mode.** The agent runs `dsh`'s one-shot headless profile only.
-   **Interactive (ACP) variant.** `dsh` has an ACP profile, but there is no `interactive_deepseek_harness()`.
-   **Checkpointing.** A sample is not resumable from an Inspect checkpoint.
-   **Sandbox identity scopes** (such as `inspect_swarm`'s users isolation). The agent raises `SandboxIdentityError` inside one.
-   **MCP servers with headers, per-server tool filters, or SSE transport** (see [MCP Servers](#mcp-servers)).
